text.p: Secessionists on the Comoros island of Anjouan stormed the airport on Friday on the third day of a general strike rapidly turning to open rebellion against the archipelago's authorities.
For a third day secessionists burned tyres and set up roadblocks, rejecting an offer by the governor of Anjouan Ahmed Abdalla Sourette for talks.
"We want separation but not talks," said a crowd at Mutsamudu, the regional capital and the Indian Ocean Comoro Islands' only deep sea port.
At least one plane was grounded as a result of the airport invasion, Civil Aviation Authorities in Moroni said.
Anjouan island, about 130 km (80 miles) southeast of the main island of Grande Comore, is poorer than Grande Comore with fewer employment opportunities for its 190,000 population.
Prime Minister Ahmed Abdou whose house was burned by a mob on Thursday denounced the Anjouan secessionists.
The unrest is ... "designed to destabilise the country ... The security forces have been given the clear mission of restoring order at all costs," he said on state-run radio Comoros on Thursday.
The Comoro islands, which have had 17 coups and attempted coups since independence from France in 1975, have this year been swept by a series of strikes by civil servants demanding salary arrears.
